findings.finding: The residual of finding 2 is real, and wider than the design's 'only for a user's first build'. quiesceSlots treats a slot whose lock file does not exist as free and holds nothing for it (tryLock returns a no-op unlock). acquireSlot walks the slots in order, skips the ones setup holds, and on reaching a slot with no lock file creates the file and takes it. So a build that starts while setup runs is steered onto exactly the slots setup cannot hold: any slot never used since it was created (every slot above the host's peak concurrency, every slot added by growing --slots, or all of them when the lock dir does not exist yet). That build can boot its VMs while flushSteps has removed the slot's WARDEN-FC jumps and bridge table, which is the window finding 2 described, for the overlap. Two smaller widenings: ownerLockDir guesses the lock dir (XDG_CACHE_HOME only when HOME is the user's), so a user whose shell sets XDG_CACHE_HOME but whose sudo resets the environment has every lock file 'missing' and loses the lock-held-before-VMMs-start check entirely; and tools/firecracker-vm/slots.sh's idle() checks carrier only, so it never sees a build that holds its lock but has not started its VMMs. Exposure needs a build to start during setup's run (seconds) and boot before setup ends; with the slot now taken before staging (finding 4), a cached raw image and a reflink copy make that plausible rather than theoretical. Preflight does not check the rules (that needs root), so nothing in the build notices. The Implementation note (docs/design/firecracker-driver.md:1224-1227) calls the residual first-build-only and says refusing 'leaves no window', which overstates it.
findings.suggestion: Close the gap rather than document it. Either (a) have setup create each missing slot lock file as the owner before trying it (MkdirAll the lock dir, open O_CREAT 0600, fchown to o.uid and the owner's gid for each file and each directory it created), so every existing slot has a lock setup can hold; or (b) add a setup gate builds respect: setup creates /run/buildwarden/firecracker-setup.lock (root-owned, 0644) and takes it LOCK_EX for the reload; acquireSlot takes it LOCK_SH (read access suffices for flock) before taking a slot and holds it until its VMMs run, failing with a 'setup is running, retry' fix when it is held. (b) also covers a wrong ownerLockDir guess and could replace slots.sh's carrier-only check. Add a fake-host test with a slot that has no lock file. Then correct the Implementation note's 'residual race only for a user's first build' and 'leaves no window'. If Jeff accepts the residual instead, the note should state it as the slots-never-used race above, and the PR body's security note should carry it.

findings.finding: setup.go belongs on the bootstrap surface. BOOT-07 defines the surface as each driver's isolation, executor delivery and start code. setup() drives the isolation reload (runSteps over setupSteps), and quiesceSlots now decides whether that reload may run at all: a change that weakens it silently re-opens finding 2, and the automated BOOT-07 check would not flag it, because rules.yaml lists only slots*.go, vm*.go and deliver_linux.go for this driver. posture.go is the same kind of code: its checks refuse setup on hosts whose firewall state would leave the slots unisolated (a11). For this diff it changes nothing (slots.go is touched, so the hint already fires); it matters for later changes on main.
